questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The main aspects of my choosing came down to the courses that was available to choose. The budget also had a big influence on my final destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. Information was mostly easy to find but sometimes not well written in English (or not English at all) which was the only obstacle.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance other than a couple of e-mail exchanges between me and the Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some things could have been a little more clearly written (like where to find the Erasmus office and how the university platform works)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Depending on your budget it was easy. I found it trough a facebookgroup specifically for danish people living Milan which made the situation alot more smooth.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive, but if you can find a several bedroom to share with others the price is fair compared to getting your own room with kitchen etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the pages was only in italian or poorly explained in English, so it could be a little hard to navigate trough.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You had to write the exact name of your chosen courses in
unimia.it
and write the ETCS points for each course

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing the Erasmus coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went well and I could register for the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure what courses you are allowed to take and what the possibilities are for taking courses from other fields. Some of the courses in Milan is between different universities which is not always allowed from your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good. All the classes I had was introduction level where you didn't need too much knowledge beforehand and I think it was mirrored well in the level of course and exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. It was less structured and no clear indication on what to read when. You kind of just have to read up on your own and not expect the lectures to match any of it

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Media theory and AI 
Anthropology of AI 
Rules reasons and norms
Artificial intelligence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in the humanistic angle of AI I highly recommend Artificial intelligence and either Media theory and AI or anthropology of AI. The last two are very close in what you learn about AI.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Painmedication is more expensive than I thought compared to Denmark. But everything else is either the same price or a little cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were several opportunities to join trips around the city/country together with other students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't go trough activities with the university but planned trips with other students trough the Erasmus WhatsApp group

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is fairly easy to take the train to other cities from Milan. I recommend Varenna, Venice, Bologna, Firenze.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took a months time to get into a new routine but Milano is fairly easy to get used to if you are used to live in a bigger city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be kinda tough (at least on the master) because it seems like most local students have their groups of friends. I was lucky enough to have a class where we had group work and that was an easy way for me to start talking to some of the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I dont know if challenging is the right word but they are less strict with administrative things. Deadlines are not as serious here which also means that it can sometimes feel a little chaotic, like there is no control over it. Its just very different for what I'm used to in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more relaxing atmosphere and that its cheap to go out and socialize with people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Say yes to day trips with new friends. don't stress about being late for class. Learn a little bit of italian beforehand - that will get you a long way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting ou of my comfortzone and getting friends from around the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier because not alot of people speak English well.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
